extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (ECRs) and other readers who perform post-publication peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for providing public, post-publication comments on scientific papers (e.g., via PubPeer or journal comment sections) aimed at ongoing evaluation, error correction, and constructive discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral, helpful, and relevant comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Give neutral, helpful, and relevant comments with the goal to open a discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to open a discussion rather than to attack. Keep tone neutral and helpful, focus on relevance to the paper, and avoid rhetoric or emotive language that could derail constructive exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: One comment per issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Give one comment per issue and avoid combining multiple observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate distinct points into separate comments so each issue can be discussed and tracked independently; do not lump several unrelated critiques or suggestions into a single comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite sources and outline reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite any sources and outline your thought process to support any constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with references, provide the logical steps or analysis that led you to the observation, and include evidence so others can evaluate your point and replicate checks if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include images if necessary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use figures, screenshots, or annotated images when they clarify the issue (e.g., pointing out a plotting error or data inconsistency); visual evidence can make comments more actionable and easier to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer actionable suggestions for change
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer actionable ways for the authors to make changes based on the feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, propose concrete remedies (e.g., alternative analyses, clarifications to methods, additional control experiments) rather than only pointing out problems, so authors have a clear path to address the concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conclusive allegations of misconduct in public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: In post-publication peer review you should avoid making any conclusive allegations as they may pose legal problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect misconduct, do not make definitive public accusations; instead, present the evidence and questions neutrally or raise concerns through appropriate channels (editors or institutional processes) to avoid legal risk and defamation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of platform moderation and participation norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms like PubPeer are open for general participation and are moderated by a team responsible for monitoring comment quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with the platform's commenting best practices and moderation policies (e.g., PubPeer Commenting Best Practices). Expect moderators to act on low-quality, libelous, or non-constructive comments and follow any site-specific rules (including anonymity/pseudonymity options).
